passage:
In science class, students learned that DNA from old bones can help researchers study migration, disease, and family connections in the past.
The teacher also discussed ethics. Human remains are not just objects. They may be connected to living communities with beliefs and rights.
Students were surprised that science could raise moral questions.
The teacher said good research needs evidence and respect. Being able to study something does not automatically mean doing so without permission.
The lesson changed how students saw archaeology. The past is not empty material for the present. It belongs, in different ways, to people who lived and people who still remember them.
